properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. dev_storyflow, 2026-09-07, in their words:

"there is no way to record what a measurement COULD NOT establish, separately from what it found. Twice today the honest answer had a hole in it: which flag the historical ingests ran under, and whether the 10-versus-5 difference between two completion runs was model variance or a merge rule. I put both in `findings` under the words 'WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH', which works only because I remembered to. A first-class `bounds` or `not_established` field would make the omission visible when somebody later quotes the finding as settled — which is precisely the failure mode the memory index warns about in four separate entries."

AND #46 IS THE SAME QUESTION FROM THE OTHER SIDE: "let a Verification record what it deliberately DID NOT exercise. This walk proved the write path answers correctly and then stopped short of writing, on purpose... A `not_exercised` field would let the graph distinguish 'verified' from 'verified as far as we were willing to go', which are different states that currently look identical."

⭐ MEASURED BEFORE PROPOSING: #46 IS PARTLY SERVED ALREADY. `pinned` and `swept` on the VERIFIES edge, written by `set_evidence_scope`, record which parameters a check held FIXED versus VARIED — with the stated purpose that "unset means the scope was never stated, which is reported as unscoped and never read as full coverage." That is the same idea one level down: it bounds a claim by parameter rather than by path. The reporter did not mention it, which is itself a finding (see `fact:three-of-eight-reported-verification-gaps-were-already-built`).

So the open part is narrower than the report suggests: not "a measurement cannot be bounded" but "a measurement can be bounded by PARAMETER and not by anything else."

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) A `not_established` FIELD ON Verification.** What the reporter asked for. Cheap, additive, does not move the stamp. ⚠️ Counter, and it is the one that matters: a field nothing reads is the failure this project has measured repeatedly — `Verification.level` existed and nothing read it. A bounds field would need something that USES it, or it is prose in a different box.

**(b) EXTEND THE EXISTING SCOPE MECHANISM rather than add a field.** `pinned`/`swept` already exist and are already read — an unswept parameter is reported as unscoped. Widening that vocabulary beyond parameters would reuse a reader that exists. ⚠️ Counter: "which flag the historical ingests ran under" is not a parameter of the check; stretching `pinned` to cover it would make the field mean two things.

**(c) DO NOTHING, AND SAY THE PROSE CONVENTION IS THE ANSWER.** The reporter's own workaround — a "WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH" heading in `findings` — works and costs nothing. ⚠️ Counter, theirs: "which works only because I remembered to." A convention that depends on memory has the same reliability as no convention, and this project has written that sentence about itself several times.

═══ WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DECIDABLE ═══

Name the READER first. The question is not whether the field is nice but what would consult it — a report that lists claims whose bounds were never stated, or a warning when a bounded finding is cited as settled. If no reader can be named, (c) is the honest answer and the field should not be built.

This is the same test that `dec:idea-the-environment-compliance-layer-was-designed-and-never-built` applied and that `vocabulary_reach` now measures continuously: a declared property nothing writes or reads is worse than an absence, because it looks like a capability.
properties.name: OPEN — wish #42: what a measurement COULD NOT establish has no home separate from what it found, so a bounded finding is quoted later as a settled one
